title: Frontend: Map Async Limit
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Map Async Limit. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement async solution({values,limit}). Asynchronously double each number with at most limit active mappings; preserve order and return {values,peak}. limit must be a positive integer. Each mapping awaits one timer turn.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Assign each input a fixed result index and let a bounded worker pool claim the next index.
alternativeApproaches: Return an async iterator for streaming output and compare input-order buffering with completion-order delivery.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty input; out-of-order completion; limit one.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
